bull_case_summary: Netflix has positive $1.525bn Q2 FCF after $5.109bn cash content spend and 13% revenue growth with 33.4% operating margin. Round two keeps the termination fee out of recurring claims and uses real post-content cash plus manageable net debt to defend ownership.
bear_case_summary: The bear accepts that actual content spending is already in FCF and cannot be deducted again. It retains declining cash and margin, fee-enhanced annual/trailing metrics and repurchases exceeding quarter cash as limits on shareholder participation.
key_points_of_agreement: Quarterly cash is positive after substantial actual content spending.
Future commitments are not all current debt and cannot be double deducted from period cash.
The termination fee sits below operating income but enhances other metrics.
key_points_of_disagreement: Whether recurring operating economics at 18.04x forecasts sufficiently compensate weaker cash conversion and capital-allocation pressure.
unresolved_uncertainties: Future content monetisation and conversion durability.
Recurring annual cash after fee/tax timing and actual repurchase discipline.
